questions.text: Which is an IT general control over computer operations?

options.A: Monitoring batch jobs and following up failures
options.B: Segregating approval of journal entries
options.C: Credit limit checks on new customer orders
options.D: A three-way match check in the ERP purchasing module

questions.explanation: Job scheduling and failure monitoring are IT operations controls; the others are business or application controls.

questions.text: Emergency changes are released to production without approval and are never reviewed afterwards. What should the auditor recommend?

options.A: Test every emergency change fully before any release to production
options.B: Allow them, but review and approve each soon after release
options.C: Ban all emergency changes to production immediately
options.D: Only allow emergency changes to be made at weekends

questions.explanation: Emergency changes are sometimes necessary; the control is a timely retrospective review and approval so none slip through unchecked.

questions.text: In purchasing, which combination of duties is incompatible and should be separated?

options.A: Creating vendors and approving payments to them
options.B: Reading system reports and printing those reports
options.C: Receiving goods and storing them in the warehouse
options.D: Attending training and signing the code of conduct

questions.explanation: One person able to create a vendor and approve payments to it could pay a fictitious vendor.

questions.text: Who should perform user acceptance testing (UAT) in the SDLC?

options.A: Business users, to confirm it meets their needs
options.B: The external auditor, as part of the year-end audit
options.C: The database administrator, just before go-live
options.D: The developers who wrote and unit-tested the code

questions.explanation: UAT is done by the business, who are best placed to confirm the system does what they need.

questions.text: A new ERP went live, but nobody reconciled the balances migrated from the old system with those loaded into the new one. What is the main risk?

options.A: Licence costs may rise in the following year
options.B: Users may need more training on the new ERP
options.C: Migrated data may be incomplete or inaccurate
options.D: The old system may never be switched off

questions.explanation: Without a data migration reconciliation, missing or changed balances can carry into the new system unnoticed.

questions.text: What does a risk-based internal audit plan do?

options.A: Audits only the areas that management selects
options.B: Audits every area with equal effort each year
options.C: Covers IT systems but not business processes
options.D: Focuses audit effort on the highest-risk areas

questions.explanation: A risk-based plan prioritises the areas where the risk to objectives is greatest.

questions.text: Audit evidence must be "sufficient" and "appropriate". What does "appropriate" refer to?

options.A: Whether the evidence is held electronically
options.B: The relevance and reliability of the evidence
options.C: Whether management agrees with the evidence
options.D: The amount of evidence the auditor collects

questions.explanation: Sufficiency is about quantity; appropriateness is about quality, meaning relevance and reliability.

questions.text: User access reviews were all signed off on time, but in several cases access marked "remove" by reviewers was still active months later. What should the auditor conclude?

options.A: Only the reviewers who signed need further training
options.B: No conclusion is possible without testing a larger sample
options.C: The control works, because every review was signed on time
options.D: The control isn't operating: review results aren't acted on

questions.explanation: A review only works if its results are acted on; signed reviews with unremoved access mean the control failed in operation.

questions.text: What should the executive summary of an audit report mainly contain?

options.A: The overall conclusion and the key findings
options.B: Every test performed, described step by step
options.C: The auditors' detailed working papers
options.D: A full list of everyone who was interviewed

questions.explanation: Senior readers need the overall conclusion and key issues; the detail goes in the body and working papers.

questions.text: What should a good management action plan for an audit finding include?

options.A: A general promise to look into the issue
options.B: The auditor's own opinion of the finding and nothing else
options.C: The names of the audit team members
options.D: A specific action, an owner and a target date

questions.explanation: Clear actions with an accountable owner and deadline make follow-up possible.

questions.text: Which COSO component covers integrity, ethical values, board oversight and "tone at the top"?

options.A: Risk assessment
options.B: Control activities
options.C: Control environment
options.D: Monitoring activities

questions.explanation: The control environment is the foundation: ethics, oversight, structure and commitment to competence.

questions.text: Which document does ISO/IEC 27001 require, listing the Annex A controls and whether each is applied?

options.A: The business continuity plan
options.B: The risk appetite statement
options.C: The Statement of Applicability
options.D: The internal audit charter

questions.explanation: The Statement of Applicability records which Annex A controls apply, their status and the justification for any exclusions.

questions.text: An accounts payable clerk changes a supplier's bank details after a phone call from someone claiming to be the supplier. Which control would best prevent this kind of fraud?

options.A: Review all supplier payments together at year end
options.B: Ask the caller to confirm the change request by email instead
options.C: Pay the supplier by cheque for the next invoice only
options.D: Call the supplier back on contact details already on file

questions.explanation: Independent call-back verification using trusted, existing contact details stops impersonation fraud before money is sent.

questions.text: What is "skimming"?

options.A: Inflating personal expense claims
options.B: Taking cash before it is recorded
options.C: Recording sales that never happened
options.D: Paying invoices from a fake supplier

questions.explanation: Skimming takes cash before it enters the accounting records, which makes it hard to detect.

questions.text: What is residual risk?

options.A: The risk left after controls are applied
options.B: The risk of choosing the wrong sample
options.C: The total risk the organisation will accept
options.D: The risk before any controls are applied

questions.explanation: Residual risk is what remains after controls; it's compared with the risk appetite.

questions.text: What does "risk appetite" mean?

options.A: The likelihood that a given risk occurs
options.B: The number of risks in the risk register
options.C: The risk that remains once all the controls operate
options.D: The risk an organisation is willing to take on

questions.explanation: Risk appetite sets how much risk the organisation will take on to achieve its goals.

questions.text: During fieldwork, an auditor finds strong signs that a manager is falsifying expense claims. What is the best next step?

options.A: Confront the manager straight away and ask for a full explanation
options.B: Ignore it, because fraud is outside the audit's scope
options.C: Escalate confidentially per the fraud procedure and keep evidence
options.D: Warn the manager's team so they can watch out for it

questions.explanation: Suspected fraud is escalated confidentially and evidence protected; confronting the suspect or spreading the news can compromise an investigation.

questions.text: What is a key benefit of using data analytics in auditing?

options.A: No longer needing to plan the audit work
options.B: Guaranteeing that no fraud has occurred
options.C: Testing the whole population, not just a sample
options.D: Replacing the controls that management operates day to day

questions.explanation: Analytics can test whole populations and pinpoint exceptions, though it doesn't replace judgement or guarantee the absence of fraud.

questions.text: Why is it important to identify the root cause of a finding?

options.A: So the audit fee can be justified to management
options.B: So the fix addresses the problem, not just the symptom
options.C: So the right person can be blamed for the issue
options.D: So the audit report looks more thorough to all its readers

questions.explanation: Recommendations aimed at the root cause stop the issue recurring; fixing only the symptom doesn't.

questions.text: An auditor finds five contractors whose contracts ended three months ago still have payroll system access, and logs show one account was used last week. What is the best next step?

options.A: Disable the accounts yourself using admin rights
options.B: Report it to management now to remove access and investigate
options.C: Note it down and include it in next year's internal audit plan
options.D: Wait and include it in the final audit report

questions.explanation: Active use of a leaver's account is urgent: escalate immediately so management removes access and investigates. Auditors shouldn't make the change themselves.
